US2011A.wouldSay: Party Rock Anthem, oh my God, everybody was shuffling in the cafeteria. This is freshman-sophomore year, Super Bass on the bus, Give Me Everything at every quince.
missing: Chris Brown feat. Lil Wayne & Busta Rhymes - Look at Me Now (2011)
Foster the People - Pumped Up Kicks (2011)
LMFAO - Sexy and I Know It (2011)
US2011A.fake: TiK ToK, Need You Now and Hey, Soul Sister are 2010 songs (one year stale, under the three-year throwback line), and there is almost no straight rap, which is what The Box actually played.
US2011A.missingScene: Southern/Houston rap radio (Lil Wayne, Wiz Khalifa, Waka Flocka, Chris Brown), country beyond one crossover (Aldean, Taylor Swift, Blake Shelton), regional Mexican banda/norteno that ran every Texas quinceanera, indie crossover (Foster the People), and YouTube virals (Rebecca Black - Friday). Christian seed is real for the Houston suburbs but not for a Catholic Latino household.

persona.name: Yadiel 'Yadi' Pena
persona.town: University Heights, the Bronx, New York
persona.background: Dominican mother, Puerto Rican father, 15 in 2014. Hot 97 and Power 105.1 for rap, La Mega 97.9 for bachata and reggaeton at home and in the bodega, Z100 in stores, YouTube, Vine and WorldStar on his phone, block parties and school dances.

Jason Derulo feat. 2 Chainz - Talk Dirty
Meghan Trainor - All About That Bass

US2014A.wouldSay: Happy, Fancy, okay, that's ninth grade, that's Z100 in the store. Propuesta Indecente, that's my mother's kitchen. But where's Bobby Shmurda? Where's Hot 97? This is what the white kids downtown were hearing.
missing: DJ Snake & Lil Jon - Turn Down for What (2013/14)
Chris Brown feat. Lil Wayne & Tyga - Loyal (2014)
Beyonce feat. Jay-Z - Drunk in Love (2013/14)
Enrique Iglesias feat. Descemer Bueno & Gente de Zona - Bailando (2014)
US2014A.fake: For 2014 it has no actual rap or R&B lead artist except Iggy Azalea, in the year of Shmoney dance, Loyal, Drunk in Love and Tuesday; Thrift Shop, Blurred Lines and Radioactive are 2013 hits.
US2014A.missingScene: Urban radio and street rap (Bobby Shmurda, Rae Sremmurd, YG, Migos, Schoolboy Q, Drake - 0 to 100, Jeremih - Don't Tell 'Em), Vine dance records (Nae Nae, Shmoney), festival EDM (Turn Down for What, Avicii, Calvin Harris - Summer), Latin urban beyond one bachata (Bailando, J Balvin - 6 AM, Dominican dembow), and Taylor Swift/Ariana Grande. Two country seeds meant nothing in the Bronx but are fair for the country as a whole.
